title: Plastics
summary: Leo Baekeland, a Belgian-born chemist who had sold his Velox photographic paper to George Eastman, used the money to set up a laboratory on his estate, Snug Rock, in Yonkers, New York. There, by carefully controlling the heat and pressure applied to phenol and formaldehyde, he made Bakelite in 1907, the first truly synthetic polymer. It found uses in the growing car and radio industries. Many other plastics followed, mass production of everyday plastic items took off in the 1940s and 1950s, and plastic waste is now a global problem.

uncertainty.note: 1907 marks Baekeland's synthesis of Bakelite; petrochemical plastics expanded into universal industrial dominance across the mid-20th century.

where.modern_name: Yonkers, New York, United States (location of Leo Baekeland's home laboratory)

importance.justification: Began the age of synthetic plastics that now pervade daily life and the environment (R4 D3 T2 L3).

beats.caption: Leo Baekeland synthesizes Bakelite in his Yonkers laboratory, inventing the first fully synthetic thermosetting plastic.
Synthetic polymers become ubiquitous in electrical wiring, automotive components, and mass-market consumer electronics.
